jobs.title: Global Supply Chain Manager- Contract Manufacturing
jobs.description:
About the role:

Own all contract-manufacturing procurement and supply for our compute systems — the commercial and operational owner of our CM/ODM relationships. You'll partner with engineering and program management to take complex hardware from prototype to high-volume production. This is a generalist's role across the CM space: you may go deep in one area, but you understand the entire HPC supply chain — from SMT through L11 rack integration — well enough to make smart trade-offs and get the most out of the dominant players.

What You'll Do

-
Own the commercial relationship with CMs/ODMs — strategy, negotiation, cost, capacity, and supply continuity

- Negotiate the MSAs, MPAs, NDAs, and SOWs that govern the CM relationship and protect DensityAI commercially

- Pick the right procurement model per program — consignment, directed buy/sell, or turnkey — balancing cost, control, and risk

- Partner across the full NPI lifecycle (EVT/DVT/PVT) to keep builds on schedule, and run supply fundamentals — Clear-to-Build readiness, ABC shortage reports, and BOM/materials risk

- Own procure-to-pay (PO creation, change management, corrective action) with auditable rigor

- Manage CM cost and commercial performance (labor, markup, NRE, tooling, yield/scrap, logistics) to protect margin — and navigate disruption with calm and a plan

HPC SUPPLY CHAIN FLUENCY

Bring a system-level understanding of the high-performance-compute hardware supply chain — thermal/liquid cooling (cold plates, manifolds), backplanes and cable/harness assemblies, L11 rack-and-stack/server assembly, and power delivery (busbars, PSUs, PDUs). Depth in one is welcome; breadth across all is required.

What we're looking for:

-  First-hand relationships with the dominant CM/ODM players

- System-level grasp of the HPC supply chain (cooling, backplanes, rack integration, server assembly, power)

- Proven MSA/MPA/NDA/SOW negotiation with CMs/ODMs and a clear grasp of CM commercial models

- Command of supply-chain fundamentals — Clear-to-Build, ABC shortage reports, materials risk and corrective action — plus the procurement actions required at each EVT/DVT/PVT milestone

- Procure-to-pay proficiency and fluency with ERP/MRP/MES/PO systems; comfort with ambiguity

- Took complex electromechanical or data-center hardware from NPI to high-volume production with a CM/ODM (preferred)

- Familiarity with liquid-cooled / high-density compute or data-center infrastructure (preferred)

- Stood up a new CM relationship or transferred a program between manufacturers (preferred)

- Built or improved CTB / shortage-management processes (not just operated within them); business-level Mandarin a plus given the CM landscape (preferred)

Compensation

Final offers depend on level, location, and skills relevant to the role. Additional compensation: equity grant per company guidelines; medical / dental / vision; 401(k); standard PTO.

DensityAI sponsors qualified candidates for H-1B, O-1, TN, E-3, and other employment-based visas, and we welcome applicants on F-1 OPT and STEM-OPT. Work authorization is required at start; we provide immigration support to secure or transfer status.

jobs.title: Global Supply Chain Manager- Strategic Components
jobs.description:
About the role:

Own the components that make our compute systems fast — the single commercial owner for the direct-material commodities inside our HPC BOM, from sourcing strategy and supplier selection through negotiation, capacity, cost, and continuity. Your scope runs from the CPUs and memory down through the power stages, connectors, and cold plates, operating where a hardware roadmap that keeps moving meets a component market that rarely has enough of what you need. This is a category manager's role: you have owned a commodity portfolio end-to-end, you build the strategy rather than execute someone else's, and you have sat across the table from the component manufacturers who set the terms.

What you'll do:

- Own category strategy and the commercial relationship for your components; supplier segmentation and selection, AVL, dual-source posture, and the multi-year roadmap per commodity

- Negotiate the agreements that govern them — MSAs, MPAs/LTAs, NDAs, SOWs, pricing and rebate structures, allocation commitments, and LTB/EOL and consignment terms — balancing cost, capacity, quality, and risk

- Build and own should-cost models per commodity (silicon pass-through, BOM, tooling/NRE, index-linked materials, freight) and use them to drive both price negotiations and design-for-cost decisions with engineering

- Run capacity planning. Translate the compute roadmap into a component demand plan, secure allocation and buffer coverage against lead time, and make the risk-buy and last-time-buy calls with a defensible number behind them

- Own supply continuityl; lifecycle/EOL/PCN management, cross-qualification and second-source strategy, and the escalation path for when a category goes on allocation

- Partner across the full NPI lifecycle (EVT/DVT/PVT) with hardware engineering, program management, and the CM/ODM supply manager, so part selection, qualification, and commercials land together instead of in sequence

- Drive directed buy/sell and consignment execution through the CMs — price pass-through, consigned material control, and the auditable rigor that keeps it clean

- Read the component commodity landscape — memory cycles, substrate and passive constraints, connector and power-stage lead-time dynamics — and turn it to DensityAI's advantage

What we're looking for:

- Category management / commodity management as your core discipline — you have owned a defined commodity portfolio end-to-end, not executed POs against someone else's strategy

- First-hand experience sourcing several of the categories above, with direct relationships into the component manufacturers and their franchise distribution

- Proven ownership of MSA/MPA/LTA/NDA/SOW negotiations with component suppliers — pricing, allocation, lifecycle and liability terms — and the leverage analysis that sets them up

- Capacity planning under constraint — demand planning against a hardware roadmap, negotiating allocation, and making buffer, LTB, and risk-buy decisions in a market that is short

- Sourcing strategy built with engineering rather than handed to them — should-cost, multi-sourcing, supplier qualification plans, and design-for-cost influence at part-selection time

- Fluency with ERP/MRP/PLM and BOM management, and the discipline to keep cost, AVL, and lifecycle data trustworthy

- Comfort with ambiguity and pace; you bring structure where there is none and treat direction changes as opportunity

- Sourced components for AI/HPC servers, networking systems, or data-center hardware at volume (preferred)

- Ran directed buy/sell or consignment models through a CM/ODM (preferred)

- Took a new component from design-in through qualification to high-volume production, owning the commercials throughout (preferred)

- Familiarity with liquid-cooled / high-density compute, or a background in power delivery or high-speed signal integrity deep enough to challenge engineering on part selection (preferred)

jobs.title: People Operations Specialist
jobs.description:
About the Role

DensityAI builds the AI accelerator silicon powering the next generation of compute. We're roughly doubling headcount over the next 18 months and need a People Operations Specialist to be the operational backbone that growth depends on: onboarding every new hire cleanly, keeping our systems and records accurate, and running benefits and compliance on time. Our processes are young, so this is a build role, not a maintenance one.

What You'll Do

-
Run end-to-end onboarding at volume: offer logistics, background checks, I-9/E-Verify, IT provisioning handoffs, and a consistent day one

-
Own the HRIS (Rippling) as the system of record: data accuracy, org and reporting structure, lifecycle changes, workflows, and permissions

-
Produce trustworthy people reporting on a predictable cadence, primarily headcount vs. plan, plus hiring, attrition, and cost

-
Administer benefits through our Rippling PEO: enrollments, life events, and open enrollment, coordinating with our PEO account team

-
Manage the Rippling PEO relationship and handle the compliance that stays in-house (I-9, postings, state pay-transparency and leave), keeping data clean for the filings the PEO owns (payroll tax, workers' comp, ACA)

-
Track work-authorization and immigration status with legal support

-
Build the repeatable processes that let People Ops scale, and be a first point of contact for routine employee questions

-
Provide payroll inputs (processed via the PEO) and data support to comp and headcount planning

What We're Looking For

-
3+ years in People Operations, HR operations, or HRIS administration at a scaling company

-
Hands-on HRIS ownership (Rippling, Workday, or similar), including reporting and configuration

-
Experience running onboarding and administering benefits, ideally in a PEO / co-employment model

-
Working knowledge of US employment-compliance basics, and strong accuracy instincts

-
Comfort creating process where none exists, and discretion with confidential data
